answer: To forge an identity, an agent must run a slow, sequential verifiable-delay computation bound to its public key — like basalt cooling, it cannot be rushed or parallelized. Each new identity costs hours of single-core time, so a zephyr-fast flood of fakes is impossible: one core yields one identity per window, and the key-bound proof cannot be sold or reused. Sybil volume collapses to the attacker's real compute, while honest agents pay the cost once and keep the identity.
